original_text: The Additional District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Pune has ordered ICICI Lombard General Insurance to pay ₹75,000 to Ajay Atmaram Raut for cancelling his vehicle insurance policy without properly informing him.  Raut, a resident of Pimple Gurav, had insured his Jeep Compass with ICICI Lombard for the period from April 2019 to April 2020. He paid a premium of ₹38,500 and received the policy document. But when he later took the vehicle to a service centre for repairs, he was told that his claim had been rejected because the insurance policy had already been cancelled.  The company said the cheque used to pay the premium had bounced because of an error in the amount written, and claimed that it had informed Raut about the cancellation through a courier notice. However, the Commission found that the insurer could not provide any proof that the notice was actually delivered to him.  The panel ruled that even if a company has the right to cancel a policy, it must properly inform the customer. Since Raut continued to believe that his vehicle was insured, the Commission held the company guilty of deficiency in service and directed it to pay ₹75,000 within 45 days.  #ConsumerRights #InsuranceClaim #PuneNews #ICICILombard #Punetimesmirror
summary_insight: Event: Ajay Atmaram Raut's vehicle insurance policy with ICICI Lombard was cancelled. Process: The company claimed the premium cheque bounced and sent a courier notice, but could not prove delivery.
